import pandas as pd
from sklearn.preprocessing import OneHotEncoder
from sklearn.compose import ColumnTransformer
from sklearn.pipeline import Pipeline
from sklearn.impute import SimpleImputer
from sklearn.preprocessing import StandardScaler
from sklearn.preprocessing import LabelEncoder
from scipy import stats

class DataCleaning:
    def __init__(self):
        self.actions_log = []

    def clean(self, data: pd.DataFrame):
        # Handle missing values in categorical variables by imputing them with the most frequent category or mode.
        for var in ["Area", "VehBrand", "VehGas", "Region"]:
            data[var] = data[var].fillna(data[var].mode()[0])
            self.actions_log.append(f"Filled missing values in {var} with mode.")

        # Convert categorical variables to numerical variables using one-hot encoding
        categorical_vars = ["Area", "VehBrand", "VehGas", "Region"]
        encoder = OneHotEncoder(handle_unknown="ignore")
        encoded_data = encoder.fit_transform(data[categorical_vars])
        encoded_data = pd.DataFrame(encoded_data.toarray(), columns=encoder.get_feature_names_out(categorical_vars))
        data = pd.concat([data.drop(categorical_vars, axis=1), encoded_data], axis=1)

        # Check and normalize/standardize numeric variables
        numeric_vars = ["IDpol", "ClaimNb", "Exposure", "VehPower", "VehAge", "DrivAge", "Density"]
        scaler = StandardScaler()
        data[numeric_vars] = scaler.fit_transform(data[numeric_vars])
        self.actions_log.append("Normalized/standardized numeric variables.")

        # Identify and remove outliers in numeric variables
        for var in numeric_vars:
            data = data[~((data[var] > 3) & (data[var] < -3))]
            self.actions_log.append(f"Removed outliers from {var}.")

        # Explore the distribution of the "ClaimNb" variable to identify potential issues with skewness or outliers
        stats.probplot(data["ClaimNb"], dist="norm", plot=pd.plotting.scatter_matrix)
        self.actions_log.append("Explored distribution of ClaimNb.")

        # Check for correlations between variables to identify potential multicollinearity
        corr_matrix = data.corr()
        for i in range(len(corr_matrix.columns)):
            for j in range(i+1, len(corr_matrix.columns)):
                if abs(corr_matrix.iloc[i, j]) > 0.7:
                    self.actions_log.append(f"Detected multicollinearity between {corr_matrix.columns[i]} and {corr_matrix.columns[j]}.")

        return data
